_comment: READ-ONLY QA tool set for bin/run-qa-agent (Epic P11-M39-E39.3) — local-agent-runner CONTRACT §4 shape, the same shape as the coding set in tools.json. This file is genuineness criterion 2's evidence: 'the run cannot mutate the working tree' is checkable HERE, from a committed file, rather than from any chat's account of itself. Enforcement layer, measured 2026-08-16 on the host against local-agent-runner 4ec1e8f: the loop advertises exactly `enabled` (tools.tool_definitions) and tool_calls._validate_call REJECTS any name outside that set as kind='unknown_tool' BEFORE tools.execute_tool is reached — so omitting write_file/edit_file/git from `enabled` is what makes mutation unreachable in a real run. NOTE the layer precisely: tools.execute_tool dispatches from its own _HANDLERS map and does NOT consult `enabled`, so a caller that bypasses the loop and calls execute_tool('write_file', ...) directly WOULD write, subject only to allow_paths. The loop is the only caller in a real run, but the belt-and-braces fields below deny the two permission-gated mutating surfaces at the handler layer as well: allow_commands is empty (empty allow denies every command, so run_command can execute nothing) and allow_subcommands is empty (deny-by-default exact membership, so git can run no subcommand). allow_paths cannot distinguish read from write — _read_file and _write_file consult the same list — so it is scoped to the repository and the sandbox mount for reading, and criterion 2 rests on the `enabled` gate, stated plainly rather than overclaimed. Path globs are copied from tools.json unchanged, including the 2026-07-13 fix (P7-M26-E26.3 escalation, tools-json-allow-paths-glob-bug): path_permitted() fnmatchcase()s against Path.resolve()'s always-absolute output, so a literal './**' can never match.
